checks.claim: Schema/conversion policy — not the file — determines column types and aggregates; sample-first inference misclassifies values beyond (and even at the edge of) its sample; failed conversions are quarantined with row/raw/expected metadata instead of silently dropped (brief §5 'do not silently delete malformed records', 'preview sampling must not be represented as proof').
checks.code_sketch: infer_naive tries int then float per value; infer_sample takes kind from head[0] of first 2 rows then forces it on all rows, quarantining failures; sums compared; asserts sums differ and a quarantine row index >= 2 exists
checks.expected_and_observed: Expected: naive yields mixed int/float/str ('1,000' stays str) and sum 57.5; sample-first forces int everywhere except declared-NA, yielding sum 54 with '3.5' (row 1) and '1,000' (row 4) quarantined. Observed exactly that; exit 0.
checks.justification: Arithmetic over explicit literal data; divergence follows from the policies' definitions and is asserted before printing OK

checks.claim: Hash-ledger status rules: outputs are 'current' only while recorded (code, env, input-content) hashes match; a source-data content change marks downstream outputs 'stale' in the same pass; a kernel restart demotes all outputs to 'unverified' and nothing auto-promotes to 'current' (brief §7; proposal §4).
checks.code_sketch: sha256 of (code, env, input) per cell record; recompute() sets status to 'stale' on any hash mismatch; restart loop sets every record to 'unverified'; assertions enforce the transition sequence current,current -> stale,stale? -> unverified,unverified
checks.expected_and_observed: baseline (current, current); after source change (stale, stale); after restart ['unverified','unverified']; all assertions passed, exit 0
checks.justification: Deterministic pure function of recorded hashes; demonstrates the rule, not any real kernel's behavior

checks.claim: Stable vs deterministic ordering distinction: sorting duplicate keys by key only (stable) preserves input order, while a total key (key + original index) is deterministic; both recorded explicitly (proposal §5, §10).
checks.expected_and_observed: stable idx [1,0,2], deterministic idx [1,0,2] for the chosen data (asserted); exit 0. Note: for this specific dataset the two orders coincide on the sorted prefix pair by construction; the check asserts the tie-break mechanism is applied and recorded, not that the orders always differ.
checks.justification: Pure stdlib sorted() semantics; honest note that this tiny case does not itself exhibit divergence — the mechanism (explicit total-order key) is what the product mandates
